name: Raan Jay Fai
vibe: Michelin-starred street stall where a woman in ski goggles cooks crab omelettes over roaring charcoal
tip: Walk-in only, so queue early. She hinted at retiring in 2024 and then denied it, so check before you go. Pricey crab omelette

name: Thipsamai Pad Thai
vibe: Bangkok's most famous pad thai since 1966, with woks flaming out front all night
tip: Order the pad thai wrapped in egg and the fresh orange juice. The queue moves fast, so go after 9pm

name: Mont Nom Sod
vibe: Retro milk bar from 1964 serving charcoal-toasted bread with pandan custard and fresh milk
tip: Get the steamed bread with sangkaya custard and a cold glass of milk. Good stop after Democracy Monument

name: Nuttaporn Ice Cream
vibe: Tiny coconut-ice-cream shophouse from 1952, tucked in a restored old-town square
tip: Coconut ice cream with sticky rice toppings. Wander Phraeng Phuthon's heritage shophouses after

name: Methavalai Sorndaeng
vibe: Old-school 1950s Thai dining room with a live band, like stepping into a Thai movie
tip: Crispy river fish with chili sauce, crab yellow curry and coconut ice cream. Go for dinner when the band plays

name: Make Me Mango
vibe: All-mango dessert café in an old shophouse, a short walk from Wat Pho
tip: Mango sticky rice and the mango shaved-ice platter. Good heat break after the temples

name: Sala Rattanakosin Eatery & Bar
vibe: Glass-walled dining room facing Wat Arun across the river, with a rooftop bar for sunset
tip: Book a window table around sunset. Try the soft-shell crab, then move up to the rooftop

name: Supanniga Eating Room (Tha Tien)
vibe: Riverside shophouse cooking grandma-style Trat recipes, with Wat Arun glowing opposite
tip: Moo chamuang and the crabmeat omelette. Reserve the upstairs terrace for sunset

name: Chom Arun
vibe: Rooftop tables staring straight at Wat Arun as it lights up at dusk
tip: Book the 5pm slot about a month ahead to catch sunset and the lit temple. You come for the view, not the food

name: ViVi The Coffee Place
vibe: Hidden riverside deck café at the end of an alley, with a front-row view of Wat Arun
tip: Grab a deck seat in late afternoon. Cheap drinks and good sunset light

name: Floral Café at Napasorn
vibe: Secret-garden café hidden above a flower shop in the 24-hour flower market
tip: Go in the evening, then walk the flower market when it's busiest. Closed Sundays

name: Steve Café & Cuisine (Dhevet)
vibe: Old wooden riverside house reached through winding alleys, serving homestyle Thai at sunset
tip: Crispy catfish salad and tamarind duck. Sit on the deck at golden hour

name: Lhong Tou Café
vibe: Chinese-style café with double-decker bunk seating and dim sum on Yaowarat Rd
tip: Dim sum plus the Chinese tea drinks. Good warm-up before the Yaowarat street-food crawl

name: Nai Ek Roll Noodles
vibe: Chinatown institution for peppery rolled-noodle soup with ultra-crispy pork belly
tip: Order kuay jab with crispy pork. It's open late, so make it your first stop on a night crawl

name: Kuay Jab Uan Pochana
vibe: Viral peppery kuay jab with a nightly queue down Yaowarat Rd
tip: Order 'everything' with crispy pork. The queue is shortest after 10pm

name: T&K Seafood
vibe: Green-shirted sidewalk seafood chaos on Chinatown's main corner, under the neon signs
tip: Grilled river prawns and steamed lime sea bass. Sit streetside after 7pm for the full neon atmosphere

name: Pa Tong Go Savoey
vibe: Fried Thai-Chinese doughnuts dunked in pandan custard, a must-do on Yaowarat
tip: Patonggo with green sangkaya dip. Share a bag while you walk the strip

name: Potong
vibe: Tasting menu in a 120-year-old family pharmacy shophouse, with a hidden rooftop bar
tip: Book weeks ahead for the progressive Thai-Chinese menu. Have a drink at the top-floor bar first

name: Mother Roaster
vibe: Secret coffee bar up the stairs of an old car-parts garage, run by a coffee-obsessed auntie
tip: Walk through the junk and climb upstairs. Try her signature brews. Daytime only

name: Such A Small World
vibe: Co-op video-game lounge with vinyl booths and free movies, hidden on a third floor
tip: Book a private lounge (from ฿400) for a date night of retro games. Closed Mondays

name: Prachak Roasted Duck
vibe: Roast-duck shophouse running since 1909, with glossy ducks hanging in the window
tip: Roast duck and crispy pork over rice. Quick, cheap lunch on Old Charoen Krung

name: The Never Ending Summer
vibe: Moody modern-Thai dining room in a converted riverside warehouse, designed by a star architect
tip: Book dinner, then stroll the Jam Factory courtyard and riverfront. Great first-date venue

name: Sirimahannop
vibe: Drinks and seafood aboard a replica tall ship moored on the Chao Phraya
tip: Sunset cocktails and oysters on deck. Book via Eatigo for deals, then walk Asiatique

name: Unicorn Café
vibe: Pastel overload: rainbow food, unicorn plush forest and unicorn onesies you can rent
tip: Rent a onesie (฿100) for ridiculous photos and order the rainbow crepe cake. Closed Mondays

name: Ojo at The Standard Mahanakhon
vibe: Wildly colourful Mexican restaurant on the 76th floor of Bangkok's pixelated tower
tip: Book a window table for sunset. Combine with the Mahanakhon glass-floor Skywalk

name: Polo Fried Chicken (Gai Tod Jay Kee)
vibe: Cult fried chicken topped with a mountain of crispy garlic, served with som tam
tip: Half chicken plus sticky rice. Eat in, then walk to Lumphini Park

name: Sretsis Parlour
vibe: Fairytale tea parlour from a Thai fashion label: pink, whimsical and very extra
tip: Afternoon tea set (from ~฿550) works well for a cute daytime date

name: Aksorn
vibe: David Thompson revives recipes from 1940s–60s Thai cookbooks, with golden-hour views
tip: Book the set menu and ask about the cookbook behind each dish

name: Mango Tango
vibe: The OG mango dessert spot, where everything is mango and the queues are full of Siam teens
tip: Order the Mango Tango set (mango, pudding, ice cream, sticky rice) and share it

name: Caturday Cat Café
vibe: Big, well-run cat café full of fluffy breeds, a short walk from BTS Ratchathewi
tip: Weekday afternoons are calmer. Order a drink and follow the cat-handling rules

name: Victory Monument Boat Noodle Alley
vibe: Canal-side alley of tiny boat-noodle bowls where people stack empties like trophies
tip: Bowls are about ฿20 each. Order 5+ each and compete over who stacks more

name: Lay Lao
vibe: Breezy blue-and-white Isaan seafood spot in hip Ari, beloved by locals
tip: Som tam with salted egg, grilled fish and sticky rice. Go before 7pm on weekends

name: Big Dog Café
vibe: Café full of huge, gentle dogs (Great Danes, Alaskans) in 2-hour play slots
tip: Reserve a slot ahead. Mornings are less crowded

name: Cabbages & Condoms
vibe: Garden restaurant decked out in condom art, where profits fund sexual-health charity
tip: Fun icebreaker date. Get the green curry and tom yum, and you get condoms instead of mints

name: Haoma
vibe: Zero-waste fine dining with vertical gardens, a fish tank and insect amuse-bouches
tip: Book the tasting menu and ask for a garden tour

name: Gaggan Anand
vibe: Rock-and-roll theatre of 20+ courses with an emoji menu and dishes you lick off the plate
tip: Book months ahead for the chef's-table experience. A once-in-a-trip splurge

name: Mae Varee
vibe: Bangkok's most famous mango sticky rice stand, at the mouth of Thonglor
tip: Grab a takeaway box of mango sticky rice and eat it on a stroll up Thonglor

name: The Blooming Gallery
vibe: Café smothered in real flowers, doing high tea that looks like a bouquet
tip: Afternoon tea for two. Open late Wed–Sat, so it works for an evening dessert date

name: Wattana Panich
vibe: Beef noodle soup from a giant pot that has simmered non-stop for 50+ years
tip: Beef or goat noodle soup. Look at the cauldron out front. Go at lunch

name: Tuba Design Furniture & Restaurant
vibe: Eat and drink inside a cluttered vintage furniture warehouse where almost everything is for sale
tip: Try the tom yum pizza and cocktails. A quirky low-key dinner date

name: Piccolo Vicolo at Wang Burapha
vibe: Restored canal-side shophouses turned into a café with a rooftop, opened 2025
tip: Matcha coconut on the rooftop. Closed Tuesdays

name: Chocolate Ville
vibe: Fake European village with a lighthouse, lake and fairy lights: peak cheesy-romantic
tip: Arrive before sunset and stay for the lights. The setting matters more than the food. A taxi ride out

name: 747 Café
vibe: Café inside a decommissioned Boeing 747 where you can sit in the cockpit
tip: Your entry 'boarding pass' includes drink credit. Pair it with an airport-side trip

name: Mustache Bangkok
vibe: Bangkok's best-known underground house/tech-house room: VOID Acoustics, a no-phones dancefloor, no song requests
tip: Fri–Sat 22:00–03:30. ~350฿ presale / 500฿ door incl. a drink. Bring your physical passport, closed shoes

name: Subwerk
vibe: Hard and industrial techno in the same building as Mustache, so you can hop between the two rooms
tip: Fri–Sat only, 22:00–03:00. 300–500฿ incl. a drink. Check IG for psytrance/DnB Saturdays

name: Elsewhere
vibe: 100-cap after-hours room running midnight to dawn: minimal and deep house in the Perlon/Giegling style for heads
tip: Fri–Sat from midnight. Go after your main night out. Check RA for lineups, 400–600฿

name: DUAL (Sacristy)
vibe: Newest underground club: an 800 m² basement with 2 floors and Funktion-One. Time Out says it's packed most nights
tip: Fri–Sat from 21:00. Tickets 300–600฿ on Ticketmelon. Entrance is in Trinity Complex, Naradhiwas Soi 3

name: Bar Temp.
vibe: Single room behind a steel door from the More Rice and Never Normal crew: house, techno and deep house on Martin Audio
tip: Wed–Sun from 19:00, until 3am Fri–Sat. Free on regular nights, 300–700฿ for events. It's about the music, not tables

name: Culture Cafe
vibe: Vinyl-only bar where minimal, dark techno and deep house play to an Old Town crowd
tip: No cover, you just pay for drinks. Open nightly until 3am. Easy follow-up after Khao San or Banglamphu

name: 12x12
vibe: Vintage living-room bar with couches, homemade plum wine and an eclectic house/disco/techno soundtrack
tip: Tue–Sat from 17:00 or 20:00. Mostly free entry, some events up to 400฿. Good low-key date bar that turns into a dance spot

name: ETA
vibe: Small, sweaty Sukhumvit room for acid, hard techno, UKG and DnB
tip: Wed–Sun from 20:00. Arrive before 22:00 to skip the cover (150–500฿ otherwise)

name: HORN
vibe: Berlin-style bunker on the 4th floor of the Silom 4 gay strip: techno and industrial with a queer, alternative crowd
tip: Thu–Sat 22:00–03:00, 400–900฿. Themed and fetish nights get announced last-minute on IG, so check first

name: Clutch Bar (The Warehouse)
vibe: Raw concrete bar in a building left empty for 30 years. Vinyl and deep house, and it can turn into a full rave
tip: Climb the stairs past the vintage and tattoo shops. Free most nights, ~300฿ on event nights. Tue–Sun

name: Tropic City
vibe: Neon tiki cocktail bar where local selectors play house, boogie and breaks on Thu and Fri
tip: Tue–Sun 19:00–02:00. Go Thu/Fri for DJs. Pair it with the Talat Noi bars nearby

name: Sing Sing Theater
vibe: Red-lantern 1930s Shanghai fantasy club by Ashley Sutton (seen in White Lotus S3), with melodic and deep house guests
tip: Tue–Sat from 21:00. Guest nights ~300฿ incl. a drink (recent guests: Chus & Ceballos). Dress up

name: Siwilai Radical Club
vibe: Stylish terrace club atop Central Embassy for disco and house, with dinner-to-dance energy
tip: Wed–Sat. Smart-casual. Have dinner at Central Embassy first

name: VOID Club
vibe: RCA's big-room club for progressive house, trance and psy, plus occasional techno takeovers
tip: Nightly 21:30–03:30, ~500฿. Age 20+, ID checked. Go for themed Halloween or progressive nights

name: Tichuca Rooftop
vibe: Jungle rooftop on floors 46–50 with a glowing LED tree, tiki drinks and tropical house DJs over the skyline
tip: Queues are long, so go at opening or book. Better with a group. Smart-casual

name: Octave Rooftop Lounge
vibe: Three open-air levels with 360° views, and DJs most nights on the top deck
tip: Arrive around 17:30 for sunset happy hour. Smart-casual. Right next to BTS Thong Lo

name: ÆTHER
vibe: New 44th-floor 360° cocktail bar with a giant silver speaker framing the skyline, one of 2026's hottest openings
tip: Arrive around 17:45 to catch sunset and the shift into night. Book on weekends

name: The NORM Bangkok
vibe: 42nd-floor design social club full of Fritz Hansen furniture, with a sunset DJ on the terrace and a private Whispering Room
tip: Book ahead on Fri/Sat and ask for the terrace. You can combine it with ÆTHER two floors up

name: Wild Iris (SO/ Bangkok)
vibe: French Riviera–style 29th-floor bar above Lumpini Park: a DJ-led main floor plus a quiet garden terrace upstairs
tip: Go at sunset. Head upstairs to talk and stay downstairs for the DJ. Signatures ~450฿

name: Sky Beach (King Power Mahanakhon)
vibe: Bangkok's highest open-air bar on the 78th floor: beanbags, a 360° panorama, and the glass Skywalk next door
tip: Book the Skywalk + bar combo ticket, go at sunset, and dress smart

name: Sky Bar (Lebua State Tower)
vibe: The Hangover II rooftop: a glowing golden dome 63 floors above the Chao Phraya
tip: Dress code is strict (no shorts or sandals). Have one drink at sunset and move on, it's pricey

name: Vertigo & Moon Bar
vibe: Open-air ledge on the 61st floor with no glass walls, just a 360° city view
tip: Closes in rain. Smart dress. Book a sunset slot

name: The Speakeasy (Hotel Muse)
vibe: 1920s Art Deco rooftop speakeasy with a retractable roof and DJs Thu–Sat
tip: Find the panel with the life-size painting of a 1920s couple. DJs from 20:30 Thu–Sat

name: Bar.Yard (Kimpton Maa-Lai)
vibe: Leafy 40th-floor backyard-style rooftop with weekly themed party nights and dance-offs
tip: Check IG for party nights. Casual-smart. Easy after dinner in Langsuan

name: SIN Rooftop (Avani+ Riverside)
vibe: Club-style 26th-floor rooftop with a big DJ booth and wide Chao Phraya river views
tip: Weekend nights for DJs. Take the hotel shuttle boat from Sathorn Pier

name: ThreeSixty Lounge (Millennium Hilton)
vibe: Glass-dome jazz lounge high above the river, with live singers and the city lights below
tip: Get a window seat. Live jazz from ~20:00. Cross by the hotel boat from Sathorn Pier

name: Bar Us
vibe: Pitch-black 14-seat 'drinking room' (#6 Asia's 50 Best 2026) with savoury cocktails served like courses
tip: Book via us-bar.com and sit at the counter. Try the Super Banana Daiquiri. Sister bar Lime by Us is next door

name: Dry Wave Cocktail Studio
vibe: Bangkok's top bar in 2026 (#4 Asia's 50 Best): lab-style 'studio' cocktails from Palm Muttarattana
tip: Find it on the 2nd floor of the Sodality building, Thonglor 13. Book on weekends

name: Lennon's (Rosewood)
vibe: Lift-access speakeasy styled as a mid-century recording studio, with 6,000+ vinyl records (#7 Asia's 50 Best 2026)
tip: Take the Rosewood lift to the 30th floor. Try the mango sticky rice Mando-tini. Pick a record

name: Bar Sathorn (The House on Sathorn)
vibe: Cocktails in an 1889 mansion (#17 Asia's 50 Best 2026), with vinyl sets from the resident DJ
tip: Order the pad-krapow Bloody Mary. Drinks 320–450฿. Next to BTS Chong Nonsi

name: BKK Social Club (Four Seasons)
vibe: Glamorous Art Nouveau bar with Buenos Aires flair (#20 Asia's 50 Best 2026), with cigar and champagne courtyards
tip: Order the Chiapas espresso martini with popcorn. Smart dress. Book

name: Opium Bar (Potong)
vibe: Secret-feeling bar at the top of a 120-year-old shophouse, reached by a tiny lift (#25 Asia's 50 Best)
tip: Enter through the Potong restaurant and take the little lift up. Book on weekends

name: G.O.D (Genius.On.Drugs)
vibe: Church-like shophouse bar from the Teens of Thailand team (#31 Asia's 50 Best 2026)
tip: Daily 19:00–01:30. Start a Soi Nana bar crawl here

name: Tep Bar
vibe: Unsigned shophouse bar with ya dong (herbal Thai whisky) shots and a live traditional Thai band
tip: There's no sign, so follow the music. Band Fri–Sun from 19:00. Arrive early, it fills fast

name: Teens of Thailand
vibe: Tiny, dark gin bar behind a heavy wooden door, a pioneer of the Soi Nana scene
tip: Look for the old wooden door with no sign. Wed–Sun. Neon sister bar Asia Today is across the street

name: Ba Hao
vibe: Neon Chinese-signage bar open to Yaowarat street life, serving herbal-medicine cocktails like a ginseng Negroni
tip: Grab a street-facing seat and people-watch. Open daily

name: Wallflowers Upstairs
vibe: Fairy-lit plant-jungle rooftop up a creaky wooden staircase above a flower café
tip: Thu–Sun only. Climb past the café. A romantic end to the Soi Nana crawl

name: Tax (Insect Bar)
vibe: Cocktails built on edible insects, every drink served with a bug snack. Great date icebreaker
tip: Start with the Bamboo Worm cocktail. Daily 19:00–00:30. Next to Bar Temp. for afterwards

name: Messengerservice Bar
vibe: 'Grocery store' cocktail bar with shelves of ingredient bottles on the 3rd floor of a heritage building (#69 Asia 50 Best)
tip: It's in the Baan Trok Tua Ngork building, 306 Santiphap Rd. Closed Mon, open late Fri–Sun

name: Mahaniyom Cocktail Bar
vibe: Thai-ingredient cocktail bar above the 100 Mahaseth Isaan restaurant (Asia's 50 Best 51–100)
tip: Eat Isaan downstairs first, then go up. Book on weekends

name: Vesper
vibe: Polished Italian-leaning cocktail bar and long-time Asia's 50 Best fixture, great for a classy first date
tip: Order a martini or one of the barrel-aged drinks. Book on Fri/Sat

name: F*nkytown
vibe: Disco-themed party bar with cocktails ranked by 'level of funk', all the way up to a Tom Yum highball
tip: Start gentle with the Pain au Matcha. Don't skip the smash burger. A short walk from Bar Us

name: #FindTheLockerRoom
vibe: Speakeasy hidden behind a wall of steel gym lockers, and you have to find the right one
tip: Go down the unmarked alley at 406 Sukhumvit 55 and slide open the right locker. Daily until 2am

name: #FindThePhotoBooth
vibe: Mint-green shophouse where a hidden button on an 'out of service' photo booth opens the bar
tip: Press the hidden button on the booth. Then go street-food hopping on Banthat Thong

name: Havana Social
vibe: 1950s Havana speakeasy behind an old phone booth: Cuban band, then salsa, reggaeton and Latin house
tip: Dial the code shown by the phone in the booth. A live Cuban band plays on weekends, so go late

name: Rabbit Hole
vibe: Craft-cocktail house behind an unmarked wooden-slat door on Thonglor, with house-leaning DJ nights
tip: There's no sign: look for the slatted wooden facade. Weekends have DJs upstairs

name: The Bamboo Bar (Mandarin Oriental)
vibe: Legendary 1953 jazz room with tiger-print booths and live bands six nights a week
tip: Book for the 21:00 set. Smart dress. Pair it with a riverside walk

name: Saxophone Pub
vibe: Old-school jazz, blues and reggae pub since 1987, full of locals and Singha
tip: Bands play nightly, so go after 21:00. Cheap and casual, no dress code. BTS Victory Monument

name: Brown Sugar
vibe: Bangkok's oldest jazz and blues club (since 1985), in a cosy Banglamphu shophouse
tip: Live music from 21:00. Combine with Adhere the 13th nearby for a blues crawl

name: Adhere the 13th Blues Bar
vibe: Shoebox blues bar where the band is practically in your lap, a Banglamphu institution
tip: Arrive by 21:30 for a seat. Cash only. 10 minutes' walk from Khao San

name: Wong's Place
vibe: Wood-panelled cult dive running since 1987 that keeps pouring long after everything else shuts
tip: Go very late (after 1am). Cash, cheap beer, self-serve fridge vibes

name: Sala Saneha
vibe: Wine bar, bookshop and a 25-seat armchair cinema in a 70-year-old building. You can bring your glass into the film
tip: Thu–Mon 18:00–00:00. Book a screening, then walk to Mustache on the same road

name: FooJohn Building
vibe: Restored 1960s shophouse with a bistro downstairs, a hidden cocktail bar upstairs and a rooftop BBQ
tip: Ask for the upstairs bar, then finish on the roof. 831 Charoen Krung Soi 31

name: Iron Balls Distillery
vibe: Steampunk gin distillery bar with the copper still right behind the counter
tip: Order the house coconut-gin G&T. The basement is booths only, good for a date

name: Firefly Bar (Sindhorn Kempinski)
vibe: Sultry jazz lounge with 370+ spirits (Asia's 50 Best 51–100) and a cricket-protein cocktail
tip: Order 'Where Is The Cricket?' if you dare. Cocktails 490–650฿. Smart dress

name: Khaoya Archive
vibe: New Ari cocktail den built on Thai local ingredients, with an ever-changing menu
tip: Wed–Sun 19:00–01:00, upstairs at No Bar Wine Bar. Try the mango-passionfruit gin fizz (420฿)

name: Maggie Choo's
vibe: 1930s Shanghai basement speakeasy (a former bank vault), with jazz bands and silk-clad performers on swings
tip: Go down the stairs under Novotel Fenix Silom. Jazz from ~21:30. Status not confirmed for 2026, so check IG first

name: Siriraj Medical Museum ("Museum of Death")
vibe: Forensic and pathology museum full of jarred specimens, crime-scene relics and conjoined twins. Bangkok's most famous weird museum
tip: Closed Tue. ฿200 for foreigners. Allow 1.5-2h. Take the ferry to Wang Lang pier. Not for the squeamish

name: Human Body Museum, Chulalongkorn University
vibe: Free teaching collection of about 2,000 real specimens, including full nervous-system dissections
tip: 9th floor of the Dentistry building. Open Mon and Fri all day, Wed mornings. Shoes off, no photos

name: Condom Museum (Dept. of Medical Sciences)
vibe: An unsigned government museum about condom testing and HIV campaigns, as odd as it sounds
tip: Weekdays only, until 14:30. Door often locked, so ask the staff by the lift. Purple Line to Ministry of Public Health

name: Snake Farm - Queen Saovabha Memorial Institute
vibe: Red Cross antivenom lab where staff milk king cobras and drape pythons on visitors
tip: Venom extraction show weekdays 11:00. Handling show weekdays 14:30, weekends 11:00. Takes about 1h

name: Chao Mae Tubtim Shrine (phallus shrine)
vibe: Canal-side fertility shrine surrounded by hundreds of carved wooden phalluses
tip: Beside Nai Lert Park Heritage Home. An active place of worship, so dress modestly. 15 minutes is enough

name: Nai Lert Park Heritage Home
vibe: Restored 1915 teak mansion and garden hidden among the skyscrapers. Quiet old-Bangkok charm
tip: Wed-Sun only. Guided tours at 9:30, 11:30, 14:30 and 16:30. About ฿250-350

name: BatCat Museum & Toys
vibe: More than 50,000 toys, said to be Asia's largest Batman collection, plus Marvel, Star Wars and life-size figures
tip: Closed Mon. ฿250 for foreigners. Take the Khlong Saen Saep boat to The Mall Bangkapi pier. Allow 1-1.5h

name: Siam Serpentarium
vibe: Immersive snake museum with 70+ live species in habitat-style enclosures and a giant snake sculpture
tip: Airport Rail Link to Lat Krabang, Exit 2. About ฿350. Good to combine with a trip to or from the airport

name: Art in Paradise (3D trick-eye museum)
vibe: Illusion art you climb into. Silly photos of you being eaten by sharks or hanging off cliffs
tip: 4th floor of Esplanade Ratchada, MRT Thailand Cultural Centre. Allow 1.5h. Charge your phone first

name: Cave Fantasy (immersive light park)
vibe: New 2026 glasses-free 3D rooms (cosmic jellyfish, glowing forest) plus a 4D flight theatre with wind and snow
tip: MBK Zone A, 4th floor. ฿499, re-entry allowed. Takes 1-2h. Open until 21:00-21:30

name: Space & Time Cube+ Digital Art Museum
vibe: 27 themed rooms of projection-mapped digital art, the closest Bangkok gets to teamLab
tip: Basement of Seacon Bangkae, a short walk from MRT Lak Song. From ฿199. Quiet walk-ins on weekdays

name: Dib Bangkok
vibe: Thailand's first international contemporary art museum, in a converted warehouse. On TIME's 2026 Greatest Places list
tip: Thu-Mon only. ฿700 for foreigners. Current show 'Giving Life' features Calder mobiles (until May 2027)

name: Bangkok Art and Culture Centre (BACC) - Bangkok Art Biennale hub
vibe: Spiral white gallery that hosts the Bangkok Art Biennale 'Angels and Mara' from 29 Oct 2026
tip: Free entry, closed Mon. The Biennale runs to 28 Feb 2027 across BACC, Wat Arun, Wat Pho, Wat Prayoon and One Bangkok

name: Bangkok Kunsthalle
vibe: Raw, burned-out former printing house turned gallery, with experimental shows, sound walks and Sunday cinema
tip: Check bangkok-kunsthalle.org for performances and biweekly Sunday film nights. Combine with Chinatown food

name: MOCA - Museum of Contemporary Art
vibe: Huge private collection of trippy, surreal Thai art. The Thawan Duchanee halls are wild
tip: Closed Mon. Allow 2h. Take a taxi from BTS Mo Chit. Good on a rainy afternoon

name: King Power Mahanakhon SkyWalk (glass floor)
vibe: Stand on a glass tray 310m up on the 78th floor. The pixelated 'Jenga' tower everyone films
tip: Open until midnight, last entry 23:00. ฿1,000 before 15:30, ฿1,200 for sunset. The I-Tilt add-on tips you 65° over the edge

name: Akara Sky Hanuman (Bangkok Reflection), One City Centre
vibe: Bangkok's newest 360° mirrored observatory on floors 58-61, with light installations, a sky bar and Thai shows
tip: Book the night SkyPass (19:00-22:00 entry), open until 02:00. Under-20s must leave by midnight. Skywalk from BTS Ploenchit

name: Baiyoke Sky revolving roof deck
vibe: Retro 84th-floor rotating outdoor deck with a buffet below. Cheesy and fun
tip: Go around 22:00 when it's less crowded. Ticket includes a drink

name: Rajadamnern Stadium (live Muay Thai)
vibe: The oldest Muay Thai stadium, with fights every night, a live pipe-and-drum band and a roaring crowd
tip: Saturday is Rajadamnern World Series (19:00-22:00). Arrive 1h early. Ringside costs ฿1,500-4,500

name: Lumpinee Boxing Stadium (Ram Intra)
vibe: The other legendary Muay Thai stadium, rowdier and with more locals betting
tip: Big cards on Friday and Saturday nights. Far north, so get a Grab. Cheaper back seats are where the gamblers are

name: Calypso Cabaret
vibe: Bangkok's classic ladyboy cabaret: sequins, lip-sync, big comedy numbers
tip: Warehouse 3. ฿900 online vs ฿1,200 at the door. Showtimes listed as 19:30/21:00 or 20:15/21:45, so check

name: Jurassic World: The Experience
vibe: Southeast Asia's first walk-through animatronic dino adventure, with life-size T-rex encounters
tip: Timed entry, about 1.5-2h. Limited run, still open mid-2026, so confirm it's running before you book. Then the Ferris wheel

name: Khon masked dance at Sala Chalermkrung Royal Theatre
vibe: Ornate royal-epic masked dance in a 1933 art deco theatre
tip: Check the schedule and book on Headout or Trazy. Show is about 1h. Sometimes cheaper with a Grand Palace ticket

name: Baan Silapin - Artist House puppet show
vibe: Free traditional Thai puppet show in a 200-year-old wooden house on a canal
tip: Show around 14:00, closed Wed (check). Tip the troupe. Canal-side coffee and slow Thonburi vibes

name: Embassy Diplomat Screens (bed cinema)
vibe: Ultra-luxe cinema with beds and private fridges, a personal server and free lounge snacks
tip: 6th floor, Central Embassy. From about ฿3,400 per bed, check the site for promos. Book a bed seat for date night

name: Enigma at Paragon Cineplex
vibe: Sofa-bed seating with massage chairs, a full bar and butler service. A peak couple flex
tip: 6th floor, about ฿4,000 per couple including a meal. Honda Ultimate Screen (from ฿2,000) is the cheaper luxe option

name: The Bed Cinema by Omazz (SF World, CentralWorld)
vibe: Electric adjustable beds with built-in massage, the cheaper way to watch a movie lying down
tip: 7th floor, SF World. From about ฿1,300. MX4D with scent effects is next door if you want chaos

name: House Samyan (indie cinema)
vibe: Bangkok's arthouse cinema for cult, festival and retro films
tip: Check the schedule for themed retrospectives. Samyan Mitrtown is open 24h for food afterwards

name: Lido Connect
vibe: Old Lido cinema turned creative venue for indie gigs, small theatre, drag nights and screenings
tip: Check the Lido Connect page for weekly events. Easy to combine with a Siam Square night out

name: Wat Pariwat ("David Beckham" temple)
vibe: Hand-carved Pikachu, superheroes, chainsaw monks and a David Beckham carving on the altar
tip: Free. Take the BRT from Sathorn. Bring your zoom lens and hunt for the hidden pop-culture figures. About 45 minutes

name: Wat Paknam Phasi Charoen (Giant Buddha & glass stupa)
vibe: A 69m golden Buddha plus a stupa with a psychedelic glass universe ceiling. Huge on TikTok
tip: Go up to the top floor of the white stupa for the green glass ceiling. Free. MRT Bang Phai or a canal boat

name: Wat Yannawa (Boat Temple)
vibe: 19th-century temple shaped like a Chinese junk ship, with a view of the abandoned Ghost Tower
tip: Two minutes from BTS Saphan Taksin. Free. Combine with the Ghost Tower view and a riverside sunset

name: Wat Chakrawat (Crocodile Temple)
vibe: Chinatown temple with a pool of crocodiles, tied to a legend of a man-eating croc the monks took in
tip: MRT Sam Yot or Ratchawong pier. Free. Combine with Yaowarat street food after dark

name: Wat Prayoon (turtle mound) - Biennale venue
vibe: Riverside temple with a man-made 'turtle mountain' full of turtles, hosting Biennale art from 29 Oct
tip: Walk across Memorial Bridge or the Phra Pokklao Sky Park. Turtle mound area opens daytime only

name: Wat Saket (Golden Mount)
vibe: Climb 300+ steps past gongs and misty waterfalls to a golden chedi with 360° old-city views
tip: Go 1h before sunset. Small foreigner fee. Huge temple fair with rides and food in November

name: Wat Arun (Temple of Dawn)
vibe: Spire covered in porcelain from old shipwrecks. Lit gold at night and a Biennale venue from Oct 29
tip: Visit in the day, then watch it lit up from a rooftop bar across the river around 19:00. ฿200 entry

name: Erawan Museum (giant three-headed elephant)
vibe: A 29m three-headed copper elephant you walk inside, up to a cosmic stained-glass dome
tip: BTS Chang Erawan. Allow 1.5h. Combine with Ancient City for a full-day trip

name: Ancient City (Muang Boran)
vibe: Huge open-air park of 100+ replica Thai palaces and temples. Rent a golf cart or bike
tip: Go after 15:00 when it's cooler (open until 19:00). Rent an e-cart. Allow 3h+

name: Sathorn Unique Tower ("Ghost Tower")
vibe: Unfinished 1990s skyscraper left to rot since the Asian financial crisis, Bangkok's eeriest skyline sight
tip: Entry is illegal and guarded. View it from Wat Yannawa or the river pier at dusk

name: Robot Building
vibe: 1986 postmodern office tower built to look like a giant cartoon robot, eyes and antennae included
tip: Photo stop only, 5 minutes. Walk from BTS Surasak or Chong Nonsi on the way to Mahanakhon

name: Phra Pokklao Sky Park
vibe: Elevated park built on an abandoned skytrain bridge over the Chao Phraya, great for sunsets
tip: Free. Go at sunset, then walk to Wat Prayoon or Pak Khlong flower market

name: Tha Prachan Amulet Market
vibe: Alleys of collectors inspecting magic amulets with loupes. Strange, intense and very local
tip: Mornings to early afternoon, busiest on weekends. Free to browse. Then grab food by the river

name: Museum Siam (Discovery Museum)
vibe: Playful interactive museum on 'what is Thai'. Also a Biennale venue from 29 Oct 2026
tip: Closed Mon. Allow 1.5h. Next to Wat Pho, so pair it with a riverside dinner

name: Jim Thompson House
vibe: A spy-turned-silk-king's jungly teak house, and the mystery of how he vanished in 1967
tip: Guided tours only (about 35 minutes). The bar and restaurant are nice for drinks after

name: Bangkokian Museum
vibe: A family's 1930s home left frozen in time: old radios, kitchens, and a doctor's surgery
tip: Free (donation), closed Mon-Tue. 30-45 minutes. Walk on to Warehouse 30 and Charoen Krung cafes

name: Warehouse 30
vibe: WWII-era warehouses turned design shops, galleries and pop-up exhibitions in the creative district
tip: Late afternoon is best. Charoen Krung street art and Talat Noi are walkable

name: Talat Noi street art & So Heng Tai Mansion
vibe: Rusting car-part alleys covered in murals, plus a 200-year-old Chinese mansion with a koi-filled dive pool
tip: Go late afternoon. So Heng Tai has a small café fee. Riverside bars nearby for sunset

name: Neilson Hays Library
vibe: Domed 1921 library with a garden café. Feels like a hidden colonial time warp
tip: Closed Mon. Small entry fee for non-members. Rotunda gallery hosts art shows

name: Museum of Floral Culture
vibe: Teak house and garden devoted to Asian flower art. Calm, pretty and a good date spot
tip: Book a tour, allow 1h. Tea in the garden afterwards

name: Jodd Fairs Ratchada
vibe: Neon night market with TikTok-famous 'volcano' leng saep ribs, bars and live music
tip: MRT Thailand Cultural Centre Exit 4. Go after 7pm and bring cash. Pairs with Train Night Market next door

name: Train Night Market Ratchada
vibe: Reopened Mar 2026 on the old colourful-tent lot. Retro stalls, cheap beer and the classic rooftop-view photo
tip: Behind Esplanade, MRT Thailand Cultural Centre Exit 3. Check their FB page before a Monday visit

name: Liab Duan Danneramit Night Market
vibe: Night market at Thailand's first theme park, with a fairytale castle, ฿30 carnival rides and BTS trains going past
tip: BTS Phahon Yothin 24 Exit 2, about a 5-min walk. Ride the Viking and go up to the castle balcony

name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
vibe: 15,000+ stalls of vintage, sneakers, plants, art and coconut ice cream. You will get lost, which is part of it
tip: Get there by 10am before it gets hot. Fri night has a 6pm-midnight market. BTS Mo Chit / MRT Chatuchak Park

name: Talad Rot Fai Srinakarin
vibe: The original vintage train market: classic cars, antiques, retro bars and huge food rows
tip: Far out, so take a Grab or the Yellow Line. Weekend nights are busiest. Behind Seacon Square

name: Chang Chui Creative Park
vibe: Hipster market built around a decommissioned airliner, with art, bars, a theatre and DIY shops
tip: Grab only. Weekends are livelier and weekdays are quiet. Closed Wednesdays

name: Siam Gypsy Junction
vibe: Gritty second-hand and vintage market under a railway viaduct, with an old locomotive at the gate
tip: MRT Purple Line Bang Son, opposite the exit. Go Wed-Sun evenings and haggle for antiques

name: Khlong Ong Ang Walking Street
vibe: Canal-side walking street with murals, lanterns, kayaks and food carts. Feels like a mini Venice at dusk
tip: Weekends only. MRT Sam Yot. Combine with Chinatown street food after

name: Asiatique The Riverfront
vibe: Riverside warehouse market with a big Ferris wheel and river breeze. Touristy, but a reliable date spot
tip: Free shuttle boat from Sathorn Pier 4-11:30pm. Ride the Ferris wheel at sunset

name: Skyflyers: Wings of Garudapterus
vibe: Asia-Pacific's tallest swing ride at 135m, spinning you out over the Chao Phraya
tip: Go after dark for the city lights. Tickets from ~฿320

name: Pak Khlong Talat Flower Market
vibe: 24-hour flower market. Mountains of marigolds and roses under fluorescent light, best after midnight
tip: Go 10pm-3am for peak trading. Buy a cheap bouquet for your date

name: Huai Khwang Night Market
vibe: Very local late-night food strip running till 5am, with Chinese-style hotpot and noodles. Few tourists
tip: MRT Huai Khwang, right by the exit. Best spot for a post-club 2am feed

name: Patpong Night Market
vibe: Knock-off market in the middle of the neon red-light strip. Chaotic people-watching
tip: BTS Sala Daeng. Haggle hard, starting at around 40% of the asking price

name: Lhong 1919
vibe: Restored 1850s Chinese trading pier with a shrine, murals, cafes and river views. Very photogenic
tip: Best late afternoon. Cross by ferry from the Si Phraya side. Closes 8pm

name: ICONSIAM
vibe: Riverside mega-mall with an indoor floating market (SookSiam) and a nightly fountain show
tip: Take the free shuttle boat from Sathorn Pier. Fountain show runs in the evenings on the river terrace

name: POP MART Global Landmark Store
vibe: Said to be the world's biggest POP MART, with Labubu shrines, a cafe and blind-box roulette
tip: 7th floor of ICONSIAM. Weekday mornings mean fewer Labubu hunters

name: Haus Nowhere Bangkok
vibe: Gentle Monster group's art-installation concept store. Weird sculptures plus eyewear and Tamburins
tip: Free to walk in. Good for photos. Pairs with POP MART in the same complex

name: Central Park (Dusit Central Park) & Rooftop Garden
vibe: New mall (Sept 2025) topped by Thailand's biggest rooftop garden: waterfalls, trails and Lumpini views
tip: MRT Silom / BTS Sala Daeng. Sunset on the roof, then Parkside Market (Michelin vendors) on LG

name: Lumpini Park
vibe: Bangkok's Central Park, with paddle boats, skyline views and giant monitor lizards strolling by
tip: Free. Go 5-7pm when it cools down. Rent a swan boat on the lake

name: Benjakitti Forest Park
vibe: Wetland forest park with elevated skywalks and skyline reflections in the lake
tip: Rent a bike and loop the skywalk around golden hour. Walkable from MRT QSNCC

name: Bang Krachao & Sri Nakhon Khuean Khan Park
vibe: Bangkok's 'green lung': a jungle island across the river with bike paths on raised walkways
tip: ฿10-20 boat from Wat Khlong Toei Nok pier. Bikes ฿40-80/day. Weekend floating market

name: Chulalongkorn Centenary Park
vibe: Sloped, award-winning design park built as a flood sponge. Locals picnic on the grass roof
tip: Combine with Samyan Mitrtown, which has 24h food courts. Best at dusk

name: Terminal 21 Asok
vibe: Airport-themed mall where every floor is a city (Tokyo, London, SF) and the toilets are a must-see
tip: BTS Asok / MRT Sukhumvit. Pier 21 food court on 5F is very cheap and good

name: Donki Mall Thonglor
vibe: Mini Japan: 24h Don Don Donki chaos, Japanese street food and snacks you've never heard of
tip: Open 24h. Great for a late-night snack run after Thonglor bars

name: EmSphere & TRIBE Sky Beach Club
vibe: Newest EM District mall with a city IKEA, IMAX and a rooftop 'beach' club with sunset parties
tip: BTS Phrom Phong skywalk. Head to the rooftop TRIBE for sunset drinks, then a concert in the hall

name: Playerbox Siam Discovery (E-Gokart & Arcade)
vibe: Air-conditioned indoor e-go-kart track, 40+ arcade machines, a VR paraglider and a private karaoke box
tip: 4F Siam Discovery, BTS Siam. Klook combo packs are cheaper. Reviews current to 2026

name: Hirono Floating Market Store
vibe: POP MART's Hirono flagship themed as a floating market, with a cafe and gallery
tip: Siam Square Soi 7. Pair it with vintage digging at Blulagoon (Siam Sq Soi 2)

name: Playsquare Laser Tag CentralWorld
vibe: Neon laser-tag arena with 20+ game modes. Competitive and silly date energy
tip: 2F CentralWorld. ~฿350/person. Also a branch at Central EastVille

name: EasyKart RCA Plaza
vibe: Real indoor go-kart track with fast 200cc karts. Race your date, then hit RCA clubs next door
tip: ~฿1,499 adult (Klook cheaper). Open until 11pm Fri-Sun. Grab there, since no BTS nearby

name: BOUNCE Trampoline Park EmQuartier
vibe: Big trampoline park with slam-dunk lanes, a wall-run zone and a giant air bag
tip: ~฿470/adult. Grip socks required. Weekday afternoons are quieter

name: Golden Axe Throw Club
vibe: Bangkok's original axe-throwing range, with beers and wooden targets
tip: ~฿500/person/hr, unlimited axes. Status not confirmed for 2026, so check their IG/FB before going

name: Stonegoat Climbing Gym
vibe: Warehouse bouldering gym with a friendly expat crowd and good beginner walls
tip: Day pass ฿300 weekdays / ฿450 weekends, shoes from ฿100. Open till 10pm. Branch at The PARQ too

name: Urban Playground Climbing
vibe: Rope and boulder walls inside The Racquet Club. The proper intro-to-climbing spot
tip: ฿495 weekday / ฿595 weekend day pass. Gear rental ฿150+

name: Flow House Bangkok
vibe: FlowRider surf wave in A-Square with a poolside bar. Wipe out, then have a beer
tip: ~US$27 per session. Hours vary by season, so check flowhousethailand.com. Last entry 1hr before close

name: Krudam Muay Thai School
vibe: Beginner-friendly drop-in Muay Thai class: pad work with real trainers and a sweaty day-one ego check
tip: ~฿599 group session via NOW Muay Thai. Wrap rental available. Go mornings before the heat

name: Bangkok Shooting Range
vibe: Fire real handguns, shotguns and rifles at an indoor range. Ages 20+
tip: Bring your passport. Daytime only, 9am-5pm. Handgun packages from ~฿2,800

name: The Last Prison Escape Room
vibe: Horror-themed escape rooms, including VR rooms. A screaming-together date
tip: From ~฿980 for 2. Book ahead. Daytime hours only

name: Harbor Island Rooftop Waterpark
vibe: Rooftop waterpark on The Mall Lifestore (opened 2025), with thrill slides and ziplines over the city
tip: Adult play ticket ~฿670 for 6h, towel and locker included. Weekdays are less packed with kids

name: Topgolf Megacity Bangna
vibe: Topgolf bays with microchipped balls, cocktails and music. No golf skill needed
tip: Book a bay for 2-6 people. Evenings have the best vibe. Next to Mega Bangna

name: Bradbury Loud Massage
vibe: Massage parlour that feels like a nightclub: DJ, live shows, and you get a massage in the middle of it
tip: 24h. Entry from ~฿350. Go after 10pm for the full chaos

name: Let's Relax Onsen & Spa Thonglor
vibe: Japanese-style onsen baths, sauna and hot-stone beds, open 24h. A slow date or recovery day
tip: Onsen all-day pass from ~฿750. Late night is quietest

name: Silom Thai Cooking School
vibe: Hands-on Thai cooking class with a wet-market tour first. You cook and eat 4-5 dishes
tip: Book a day ahead. Morning, afternoon and evening slots, ~฿1,000-1,500. Evening class makes a good date

name: Chao Phraya Express Boat (Orange Flag)
vibe: Ride the river with locals past temples and palaces for pocket change. The cheapest sightseeing in Bangkok
tip: Board at Sathorn Pier (BTS Saphan Taksin). Flat fare ~฿16. Ride to Tha Chang for Wat Arun views at sunset

name: Khlong Saen Saep Canal Boat
vibe: Rough-and-tumble commuter canal boat with tarp splash guards and a jump-on-jump-off crew. Real Bangkok
tip: From Pratunam pier west to Phan Fa (Old Town). ฿10-20. Avoid rush hour

name: Woot Woot Vintage (Warehouse 30)
vibe: Curated vintage and retro homeware inside the Warehouse 30 creative complex
tip: Charoen Krung Soi 30. Pair with cafes on Charoen Krung and Talat Noi

name: Fumiikii Tokyo
vibe: Japanese-curated vintage shop in hip Ari. Ari's cafes and street food are around the corner
tip: Ari Soi 2, BTS Ari. Go late afternoon, then have dinner in the Ari sois

name: Treasure Factory Phra Khanong
vibe: Japanese second-hand megastore for branded clothes, gadgets and random Japan finds at low prices
tip: Near BTS Phra Khanong. Several branches. Check the 'new arrivals' racks

name: 2nd STREET CentralWorld
vibe: Japan's biggest resale chain: racks of pre-loved Comme des Garcons, Stussy and designer bags in a mall
tip: 5th floor, 10am-10pm. Shoes and bags sections are the strongest; weekday evenings are calmer

name: 2nd STREET Siam Discovery
vibe: Brand-new 2nd Street (opened Sept 2026) right on the BTS, fresh racks of Japanese pre-loved fashion
tip: Mezzanine floor. New stores get stocked heavy at launch, so go early before the good stuff is picked

name: 2nd STREET Big C Rama 4
vibe: The first and biggest 2nd Street in Thailand, a full floor of Japanese resale fashion and luxury
tip: 1st floor of Big C Rama 4, 10am-8pm. Bigger than the mall branches, so best for a long dig

name: Treasure Factory Sukhumvit 39
vibe: Japanese reuse store stuffed with brand clothes, bags, cameras and homeware that Phrom Phong expats sold off
tip: 10am-7pm. Expat area means good branded stock; you can also sell your own stuff here 10am-6pm

name: Treasure Factory Cloud 11
vibe: Newest Treasure Factory inside the Cloud 11 creative complex, combine with a rooftop flea when one is on
tip: 10am-8pm, near BTS Punnawithi. Check Cloud 11 events: Made by Legacy flea markets have run on its rooftop

name: Treasure Factory Bang Khae
vibe: West-side Treasure Factory with less competition from other thrifters, so better odds on gems
tip: 10am-8pm, near MRT Lak Song/Bang Khae area. Good for appliances, kitchen gear and Japanese brands

name: Komehyo CentralWorld
vibe: Japan's legendary second-hand luxury house: authenticated Rolex, Hermes and LV you can actually touch
tip: 2nd floor of Central@centralwOrld. Window shopping is free; book a private room if you want to sell

name: RAGTAG One Bangkok
vibe: Tokyo's cult designer consignment store: 70% Japanese labels like Yohji, Issey and Undercover
tip: Opened mid-2025 in One Bangkok. Prices run 600 to 500,000 baht; the oversized pieces sell out fastest

name: Bangsue Junction (Red Building / Tuek Daeng)
vibe: Six air-conditioned floors of vintage denim, band tees, military jackets, cameras and antiques by Chatuchak
tip: Go Fri-Sun after 11am when most shops open. Tees 100-200 baht, jackets 1,000-2,500. Start at top floor

name: Mixt Chatuchak
vibe: Indoor, air-conditioned side mall of Chatuchak with secondhand bags, clothes and anime figure stalls
tip: 2nd floor is the secondhand and figures floor. Great escape from JJ heat; open daily, so weekdays work too

name: Pattavikorn Market (Nawamin 72)
vibe: Gritty bale-dump flea market: fresh sacks get ripped open and everyone dives in for 5-25 baht pieces
tip: Tue night and Wed morning bring fresh bales. Bring small cash, sanitiser and a big bag; no haggling

name: Talat Khlong Thom (Saturday flea)
vibe: Chaotic old-Bangkok junk market: tools, watches, film cameras and random gadgets spread on tarps
tip: Saturday evening is the big night. Dig the ground-level tarps, bring small notes, walk from MRT Sam Yot
hours: Daily shops 7:30-19:00; main flea Sat evening

name: Mega Plaza Saphan Lek
vibe: Bangkok's Akihabara: floors of anime figures, Gundam, Pokemon cards, retro consoles and used cameras
tip: Walk a whole floor before buying, many shops sell the same thing. Prize figures 240-400 baht. Closes 7:30pm

name: Wang Lang Market
vibe: Riverside alley maze with some of Bangkok's oldest secondhand clothes stalls plus killer street snacks
tip: Take the boat to Wang Lang pier. Most clothes 100-200 baht; go late morning before the lunch crush

name: Shinjuku Outlet Lat Phrao
vibe: Multi-floor Japanese and Korean used clothing sold by weight, from 30-39 baht per 100 grams
tip: Weigh your basket before the till. New stock drops every couple of weeks; winter coats are the steal

name: Sakura Japan Second-hand Market
vibe: Warehouse of Japanese import junk: kawaii plushies, ceramics, homeware and clothes, often by the kilo
tip: Near BTS On Nut, 11am-9pm. Lots of it is 50-100 baht per kg; fixed-price items are tagged separately

name: Papaya Studio
vibe: Giant antique warehouse of diner chairs, neon signs, old movie props and retro toys; feels like a film set
tip: Free to browse, 9:30am-7pm. Trinkets around 1,000 baht, furniture much more. Bring a camera, it's very photogenic

name: Lucky Home Samrong
vibe: Japan shipping-container warehouse: crates of digicams, film cameras, lenses, guitars and vinyl
tip: 10 min walk from BTS Samrong. Digicams can be under 300 baht; test everything, no returns

name: Dasa Book Cafe
vibe: Three cosy floors of 18,000 used books in English and European languages, with coffee
tip: Between Soi 26 and 28. Trade in your old books for credit; open daily 10am-8pm

name: Classic Movie Poster
vibe: Tiny shop of hand-painted Thai movie posters from the 1950s on, including Thai versions of Hollywood hits
tip: Next to Lido, Siam Square Soi 2; opens around 2pm. Ask for original painted theatre posters

name: Tokyo Joe
vibe: Two floors of vintage and luxury resale: designer tops downstairs, sneakers, jeans and coats upstairs
tip: Daily 10am-8pm. They also buy branded vintage, so bring pieces to trade

name: (un)FASHION Vintage S39
vibe: Leather heaven: vintage cowboy boots, belts and Italian bags plus Japanese imports, with a cafe vibe
tip: Behind EmQuartier, 10am-8:30pm. Original Ekkamai 10 branch gets new stock on Wednesdays

name: Labellist Vintage Vibes
vibe: Museum-grade vintage Chanel, Hermes and 60s-2000s designer pieces in a luxe mall
tip: 2nd floor Gaysorn. Mostly for looking unless you have a fat budget; call ahead to confirm it's open

name: Again & Again Vintage (Suan Plern Market)
vibe: Colour-sorted racks of 70s boho vintage inside a quirky little retro market on Rama 4
tip: Pieces around 500-5,000 baht. Pair with a wander around the rest of Suan Plern market

name: Zudrangma Records
vibe: Legendary crate-digger shop for Thai funk, molam and luk thung; the Studio Lam bar is right there
tip: Wed-Sun noon-8pm, closed Mon-Tue. Lost & Found Japanese vintage clothing sits upstairs

name: Fortune Town Record Shops (DP Music, Coconut Records)
vibe: A whole floor of an old IT mall turned vinyl hub: original Thai luk thung pressings, 60s-80s rock and soul
tip: 3rd floor, roughly 11:30am-8pm. MRT Phra Ram 9. Coconut for original pressings, DP Music for Thai rarities

name: Format BKK
vibe: Ari record shop for off-mainstream Thai and international vinyl plus used 60s-90s LPs and workshops
tip: Daily 11am-8pm. Combine with Ari cafe hopping; check their IG for listening sessions and workshops

name: HAVE YOU HEARD? Records
vibe: Charoen Krung record store with indie, house, techno and world music, open till midnight on weekends
tip: Fri-Sat noon-midnight, Wed/Thu/Sun to 8pm, closed Mon-Tue. Good pre-drinks stop on the creative strip

name: More Rice Record Store
vibe: House and techno vinyl shop with DJ gear, merch and zines; the city's club-head record spot
tip: Tue-Fri 1-8pm, Sat 3-8pm, closed Sun-Mon. Ask staff what's on at the clubs this week

name: Sassysoul Record
vibe: Chinatown vinyl shop for anime and film soundtracks, Japanese city pop, Disney and R&B
tip: Daily 11am-7pm on Yaowarat 27. Hit it before Chinatown street food comes alive at night

name: Get Back and Jude Records
vibe: 7-inch singles, 60s rock, Britpop, disco and Thai alternative in a Chinatown shophouse
tip: Daily 11am-8pm. Pairs well with Sassysoul for a Chinatown vinyl crawl

name: Cassette Shop
vibe: Tiny shop of tapes plus refurbished Walkmans and decks; peak retro analog nerd energy
tip: Mon-Sat 11am-7pm, closed Sun. A refurbished Walkman makes a great gift

name: Vinyl Die Hards
vibe: Classic rock, soul and soft pop LPs from the 60s-80s, a solid dig before Rot Fai Srinakarin
tip: Daily 10am-6:30pm. Go late afternoon, then head to the Srinakarin train market when it opens

name: Vinyl & Toys Cafe
vibe: Late-night cafe with 500+ records, vintage toys and old Sega consoles to nerd out over
tip: Listed as open all day. Good late-night hang; spin records over coffee

name: Tay Flea Market (seasonal)
vibe: Seasonal 200+ vendor vintage and collectibles flea with giant sculptures, pets welcome
tip: Pop-up seasons run a few days, 4-11pm, free entry. Watch their socials for the next season dates

name: Little Zoo Garden Capybara Cafe
vibe: Capybaras with their own pool, plus meerkats, wallabies, deer and corgis. Bangkok's best-known capy spot.
tip: 450 THB with drink, cookie and treat basket, unlimited time. Walk-in. Weekend afternoons get packed.

name: Capybara Coffee Bangkok (Ekkamai)
vibe: Timed capybara sessions on the 2nd floor of Union Ekkamai 61, with meerkats, monkeys and ducks too.
tip: 400 THB for 30 min, drinks extra. Book on WhatsApp +66 88 179 3315, especially weekends.

name: Capybara Coffee Bangkok (Silom)
vibe: Tucked-away alley branch of the viral capybara cafe, smaller and more intimate than Ekkamai.
tip: 400 THB per 30-min slot, drinks from 80 THB. Book ahead; check pin on Google Maps, alley is hidden.

name: BlueGold Coffee & MiniZoo
vibe: Big cafe with a capybara family, camels, goats, deer and parrots out back. Feels like a mini safari.
tip: No entry fee, just order at the bar to get in. Civet coffee is their thing; skip it if welfare bothers you.

name: All Weather Farm
vibe: Organic farm cafe on the far south edge of Bangkok with capybaras, goats, pigs and chickens.
tip: Free entry, no minimum order. Go weekday mornings; closed Mondays. Grab/car needed.

name: Cafe De Musketeer
vibe: Sprawling family-style garden cafe on the west edge where you can watch and feed capybaras.
tip: Free entry, cheap animal feed. Capybaras come out from about 3pm. Busy and noisy with kids on weekends.

name: Little Zoo Cafe (On Nut)
vibe: Old-school exotic pet cafe: raccoons, fennec foxes, meerkats, owls, corgis and hedgehogs.
tip: About 390 THB incl. drink and snack. Some reviews raise welfare concerns about the exotic animals.

name: Dog Country Cafe (Chatuchak flagship)
vibe: Massive dog resort with 400+ dogs, a big-dog zone, pool, plus cats, rabbits, goats and pigs upstairs.
tip: 300 THB unlimited play with a drink. Shoe covers given. Easy add-on to a Chatuchak market day.

name: Dog in Town Ari
vibe: Bright backyard-style room full of fluffy malamutes, samoyeds and goldens who will climb on you.
tip: 350 THB with one drink, unlimited stay, walk-in. Weekday afternoons are calmest.

name: TrueLove @ Neverland
vibe: Session-based husky cafe where 20+ Siberian huskies get released into the room at once. Pure chaos.
tip: Sessions 1pm and 4pm. 350 THB with drink and cake. Cash only, first come first served.

name: Corgi in the Garden
vibe: Garden cafe packed with name-tagged corgis waddling around. TikTok corgi content factory.
tip: 300-350 THB with drink. Closed Mondays. Near BTS Wutthakat; go at session start for max zoomies.

name: The Wrinkles Pug House
vibe: Tiny weekend-only pug cafe. A room of snorting wrinkly pugs for under 200 baht.
tip: 169 THB with drink and snack. Fri-Sun only, booking required via Facebook or 083-177-8483.

name: Rabbito Cafe
vibe: Around 40 free-roaming rabbits hopping around your feet in a homey cafe.
tip: About 100 THB entry, no time limit. Wear clothes you don't mind getting fur on.

name: Mohu Mohu Cat Cafe
vibe: Japanese-style cat cafe with about 20 rescued strays and a proper Japanese menu.
tip: Pay per 10 min (25-30 THB), waived if you spend more on food. Book for weekends; no kids under 10.

name: Catsanova Adoptable Cat Cafe
vibe: Non-profit cat cafe where all 20+ cats are up for adoption. Feel-good welfare-first option.
tip: 150 THB, exchangeable for food. Reservation only. Closed Tuesdays.

name: Brown Matcha House
vibe: There is a Batmobile parked inside a matcha cafe. Vintage sci-fi room, seriously good matcha.
tip: Daytime only, closes 4-5pm. Combine with an Old Town walk.

name: Dine in the Dark (Sheraton Grande Sukhumvit)
vibe: Four-course dinner in total blackness, served by visually impaired guides. Mind-bending date night.
tip: Book well ahead on +66 2 649 8888. Try the Surprise menu and guess what you ate.

name: Alien Bangkok
vibe: New 'fine bistro' designed like dining in outer space, cosmic murals and all.
tip: Pricey, dinner from 17:00. Order the onion tarte tatin with chicken liver pate. IG @alien_bangkok.

name: Mocking Tales
vibe: Wizard-world fantasy cafe with smoking potions, erupting 'Inferno Mountain' desserts and candy-floss drinks.
tip: Closed Tuesdays. Order the Inferno Mountain for the video. Far west, go by Grab.

name: The Ghost House
vibe: Cafe run by the host of Thailand's famous ghost radio show, full of spirit-house and creature props.
tip: Open till midnight on weekends, perfect before RCA clubs. Try the 'Ghost Coffee' or honey toast.

name: Kid Mai Death Awareness Cafe
vibe: Death-themed Buddhist cafe: lie in a coffin for a discount, then do one of the horror escape rooms.
tip: Status has been patchy over the years, check Facebook or KKday before you go. Escape rooms from ~690 THB.

name: Natura Cafe at Poomjai Garden
vibe: Hidden jungle cafe through a bamboo village, with a canal pavilion. Feels hours from Bangkok.
tip: Daytime only. Dog-friendly. Pair with the boat to Wat Paknam's giant Buddha nearby.

name: HILLING Glamping Cafe
vibe: Glamping-style cafe with tents and rustic camp gear, right in the middle of Sathorn.
tip: New for 2026. Daytime coffee and bakery; best late afternoon light.

name: Patom Organic Living
vibe: Tiny glass greenhouse cafe in a residential garden, all plants and organic drinks.
tip: Only about 25 seats, go on a weekday morning. Closed Tuesdays.

name: San Rafael Cafe
vibe: Giant wine-glass-shaped wooden pavilions, seat pods, an indoor waterfall and a 360-degree brew bar.
tip: Opens 7am, go early for empty photo spots. Far west, take a Grab.

name: Featherstone Cafe
vibe: Apothecary-style vintage cafe with colorful 'potion' sparkling drinks served in lab flasks.
tip: Get the colored sparkling 'potions' for photos. Weekday afternoons are quietest.

name: Jeh O Chula
vibe: Legendary late-night Tom Yum Mama: a giant pot of instant noodles loaded with seafood and crispy pork.
tip: Use the QueQ app; waits hit 2 hours. Mama pot (250-300 THB) feeds two. Go right at 4pm or near midnight.

name: P'Aor Tom Yum Noodles
vibe: Creamy tom yum noodles topped with a whole lobster or giant river prawns. Mukbang royalty.
tip: Lobster bowl is the flex; regular bowls are cheap. Expect a queue at lunch.

name: Go-Ang Kaomunkai Pratunam (Pink Chicken Rice)
vibe: The famous pink-shirt chicken rice shop: Bib Gourmand Hainanese chicken, packed day and night.
tip: Cheap and fast, line moves quickly. Open late, great after Pratunam shopping.

name: Yaowarat Toasted Bread
vibe: Charcoal-toasted buns oozing custard and pandan, under 30 baht. Lines go past midnight.
tip: Night-only stall on Yaowarat Rd. Get pandan and Thai tea custard. Bring cash.

name: Spire Rooftop Bar (Dusit Thani)
vibe: Newest big Silom rooftop on the rebuilt Dusit Thani, looking straight down onto Lumpini Park's greenery.
tip: Arrive before sunset for magic hour over the park. Try the Proton Candy cocktail (฿420). Smart casual.

name: Sanctuary Bangkok (InterContinental Sukhumvit)
vibe: Tichuca's calmer little sister: bamboo roof, greenery and open sky on the 34th floor.
tip: Few seats, so book ahead. Good pre-dinner or nightcap stop near BTS Thong Lo. Closes if it rains.

name: Sato San (Moxy Ratchaprasong)
vibe: Japanese-Isan 'Electric Carnival' rooftop with a red-glowing bamboo arch and a DJ facing the city lights.
tip: Take the lift from the 9th-floor Moxy lobby to 32F. Sunset aperitifs, then DJ sets late. Opened NYE 2025.

name: Piscari (Andaz One Bangkok)
vibe: Mediterranean rooftop that goes calm at sunset, party with DJ sets after dark, plus a hidden speakeasy corner.
tip: Come for golden hour, stay for the DJ. Ask about the secret speakeasy room for a quieter drink.

name: Starlight Rooftop Bar (Mercure Surawong)
vibe: Gem-themed 31st-floor rooftop with 360 views from the river to Silom, and Thai-spirit cocktails.
tip: New for 2026 and still under the radar, so easy to get a good seat at sunset. Mid-range prices.

name: Nobu Bangkok Rooftop Bar (The Empire)
vibe: Lounge, whisky bar and rooftop on floors 57-60 of The Empire with full 360 skyline views.
tip: Dress sharp. Go up for a drink only if dinner is too pricey. Right by BTS Chong Nonsi.

name: Red Sky (Centara Grand CentralWorld)
vibe: Classic 56th-floor sky bar under a red arch, right above CentralWorld's lights.
tip: Smart casual. Combine with the Centara pool party on 26F, which sometimes moves its afterparty up here.

name: Penthouse Bar + Grill (Park Hyatt)
vibe: Three-level penthouse with a 70s-style speakeasy, live music and an open-air terrace on top.
tip: Direct walkway from BTS Phloen Chit. Book the terrace for sunset; dress smart.

name: Paradise Lost (Siam@Siam Design Hotel)
vibe: Quirky 25th-floor rooftop garden over Siam with jungle-ish decor and fair prices.
tip: Steps from BTS National Stadium. Good cheaper warm-up before heading out.

name: Yao Rooftop Bar (Marriott Surawongse)
vibe: 32nd-floor Chinese-styled rooftop with lanterns and sweeping views over the river bend.
tip: Sunset is the move. Walkable to Talat Noi and Charoen Krung bars afterward.

name: CHAR (Hotel Indigo Wireless Road)
vibe: Relaxed 26th-floor rooftop with good-value cocktails and a casual crowd above Wireless Road.
tip: Happy hour early evening; a low-key alternative to the pricier Ploenchit sky bars.

name: ABAR Rooftop (Marriott Marquis Queen's Park)
vibe: 38th-floor rooftop overlooking Benjakitti and Benjasiri parks, gin-focused bar with a big terrace.
tip: Sunset over the parks is the reason to go. Short taxi from BTS Phrom Phong.

name: Above Eleven (Fraser Suites Sukhumvit)
vibe: Peruvian-Japanese rooftop on 33F with a lively weekend crowd and DJ-driven nights.
tip: Smart casual enforced. Pair with Pastel and Nao nearby for a Soi 11 crawl.

name: Throwback Rooftop (Silom Edge)
vibe: Low-rise 9th-floor rooftop with no hotel stiffness, right at the Silom-Rama IV junction.
tip: Cheaper casual drinks before a Silom night. Steps from BTS Sala Daeng and MRT Silom.

name: Pastel Rooftop Bar (Aira Hotel)
vibe: Pastel-and-neon Mediterranean rooftop on 22F built to run from dinner into a party.
tip: Busiest on weekends. Watch their Instagram for themed DJ nights and the NYE party.

name: Cloud 36 (Chatrium Riverside)
vibe: 36th-floor river-bend rooftop with 360 views of the Chao Phraya and Asian-spiced cocktails.
tip: Live music and guest shifts on select nights. Smart casual. Quieter than the big-name sky bars.

name: Swing Bar by ChingCha
vibe: Hostel rooftop looking straight at the Giant Swing and temple roofs, with ฿100 beers.
tip: Cheapest rooftop sunset in the old town. Cocktails from ฿150. Easy walk to Phra Sumen bars.

name: YABAR Secret Bar & Rooftop
vibe: Hidden bar and rooftop you reach through Olive Kitchen on Soi Rambuttri, open till 2:30am.
tip: Enter via Olive Kitchen. Closed Wednesdays. Jumbo Singha ฿160, Long Island ฿169.

name: Brewski (Radisson Blu Plaza)
vibe: 30th-floor rooftop beer bar with American craft and Belgian classics plus a party feel.
tip: Best rooftop for beer people. Easy walk from Asok BTS / Sukhumvit MRT.

name: Electric Sheep (The Warehouse Talat Noi)
vibe: Blade Runner-styled 4th-floor rooftop with big cushions and ferment-heavy food from the J'AIME chefs.
tip: Closed Mon-Tue. Last orders 10:30pm, so go early, then head downstairs to Clutch Bar.

name: Centara Grand Pool Party (26F Pool Deck)
vibe: Regular Saturday pool party with house and deep house DJs on a 26th-floor deck above CentralWorld.
tip: Roughly monthly Saturdays 3pm-10pm, from ฿600 (early bird cheapest). Next: 31 Oct, 21 Nov, 12 Dec 2026.

name: WET Pool at W Bangkok (Beats by the Pool)
vibe: W's poolside party series with cabanas, Bangkok Invaders DJs and a big Songkran edition.
tip: Monthly-ish, mostly hip-hop leaning. Book a cabana for groups. Check W Bangkok IG for dates.

name: Mad Stash x Westin Pool Party
vibe: Westin Grande's poolside series with melodic techno, deep house and afro house selectors.
tip: Usually a Saturday afternoon, tickets around ฿900. Listed on Resident Advisor, so check RA for next date.

name: Ambar Rooftop Pool (Four Points Sukhumvit 15)
vibe: Affordable 8th-floor poolside rooftop with a first-Saturday pool party mixing afro, deep house and hip-hop.
tip: Cheapest pool party in central Sukhumvit. First Saturday of the month; confirm on their IG.

name: Cloud 11 Rooftop Park
vibe: Thailand's biggest elevated park (Snohetta), now hosting big open-air parties like Kolour's 15th birthday.
tip: Kolour 15 Years (Richie Hawtin, Nora En Pure): Sat 21 Nov 2026, 2-10pm, from ฿1,600. Near BTS Punnawithi.

name: Baccarat
vibe: Glossy New York-style club spinning afro, melodic and tech house mixed with hip-hop till 4am.
tip: Queues before opening on weekends. Book a table for groups. Dress sharp.

name: APT 101
vibe: 70s New York apartment-style bar: vinyl arcade with pool table, chatty pantry, and a club room with tech and afro house.
tip: Hours vary, call 02-821-5813 or check apt101club.com. Balcony has city views.

name: Salon Kiku
vibe: 4th-floor DJ bar digging jazz, soul, Thai funk, global grooves and house.
tip: Check IG for guest selectors. Good warm-up before Thonglor clubs.

name: Decommune
vibe: Bare-walled underground club and culture room in Liberty Plaza: left-field electronic, gigs and film nights.
tip: Wed-Sun 7pm-midnight. Drinks are cheap for the area. Follow their IG for line-ups.

name: OBi Record Bar
vibe: Japanese jazz-kissa style vinyl bar where bartenders take turns as DJs, jazz drifting into soul and hip-hop.
tip: Thu-Sat 6pm-1am, guest DJ some Wednesdays. Budget ฿500-1,000 per person.

name: Modern-Day Culture
vibe: Vinyl bar run by 20-year record collectors, with Thai-herb cocktails and natural wine.
tip: Right by BTS Ekkamai. Order the herbal cocktails. Confirm days before going.

name: Soulmate Listening Bar
vibe: Old house turned living-room listening bar with vinyl, occasional live acts and a front garden.
tip: Closed Wednesdays. Weekends fill up, so reserve via Instagram or Line.

name: aftersun Listening Bar
vibe: 70s-toned listening bar in an old dorm room with a different vinyl DJ nightly and 10 rotating craft taps.
tip: Far west, so make it a mission night. Closed Tuesdays. Dig the record crates for sale.

name: Yayyyyy Record Bar
vibe: Shophouse-sized wooden bar with 1,500+ records, highballs and easy cocktails.
tip: Tue-Sun 6pm-midnight. Pair with Bar Temp. and the Phra Sumen bars for an old-town crawl.

name: Long Play Music and Bar (Josh Hotel)
vibe: Warm speakeasy-style vinyl room with a cinema projector and jazz and vinyl DJs.
tip: 2F of Josh Hotel, Ari Soi 4. Start the Ari bar hop here. Closed Mondays.

name: Nao Bar
vibe: Locked-door Japandi speakeasy in an old office, where the kitchen counter is the bar.
tip: Call the front phone to get in. Try the Stay Alive (wasabi-cucumber gin). Check days, some Sundays closed.

name: Residents Only
vibe: Kowloon Walled City-themed cocktail bar: deliberately raw, chaotic and creative.
tip: Thonglor Soi 17. Good stop between Thonglor bars and clubs.

name: Chinatown Yacht Club
vibe: Gritty NY-style dive in a historic shophouse with a rooftop garden, B-sides and 90s boom bap.
tip: Hit Soi Nana Chinatown on a Friday: this, Xin Xe Goi and Bar Temp. are all within a few minutes.

name: Xin Xe Goi
vibe: Three-storey neon bar with a rabbit mural, Thai-Chinese small plates and street views from the top.
tip: Grab the top floor for people-watching over Soi Nana.

name: Hair of the Dog (Phrom Phong)
vibe: Two-time best beer bar winner: heavy music, macabre decor, new brews and blind tastings.
tip: Mon-Sat. Good pre-game before Sukhumvit clubs.

name: Two Palms Taproom
vibe: Local craft taps inside a 200-year-old colonial building near Phra Arthit.
tip: Closed Tuesdays. Combine with Decommune and Phra Arthit's riverside bars.

name: Yankii Robatayaki & Bar
vibe: Charcoal grill upstairs, open karaoke bar downstairs: sing in front of strangers, no time limits.
tip: No bookings and no private rooms, so arrive early on weekends. Near BTS Phrom Phong.

name: Haru Ranman Comic Cafe & Bar
vibe: 24-hour Japanese manga cafe with karaoke rooms and 30,000 manga volumes.
tip: Open 24 hours, so a fun 3am landing spot after clubs.

name: Pickle.BKK
vibe: Two-level LGBTQ+ art-music-fashion space with a 90s-vibe DJ and a quirky vintage TV corner.
tip: Fills up late. Easy walk from BTS Sala Daeng and the Silom Soi 4 strip.

name: Mae Nak Shrine at Wat Mahabut
vibe: Shrine to Thailand's most famous ghost, piled with dresses, baby toys and lottery wishes by a canal
tip: Free. Go the evening before a lottery draw when it stays open late and gets packed. BTS On Nut, Soi On Nut 7

name: Trimurti Shrine (the Love Shrine)
vibe: Singles in red offer nine red roses to a Hindu god outside CentralWorld, hoping to find love
tip: Thursday 9:30pm is the lucky slot. Roses and red incense sold on site. Ganesha shrine is next door

name: Lakshmi Shrine (Gaysorn rooftop)
vibe: A gold goddess of wealth hidden on the 4th floor terrace of a luxury mall, above the traffic
tip: Free. Take the lift to 4F Gaysorn Village. Offer pink lotus and sugarcane juice for money luck

name: Huai Khwang Ganesha Shrine
vibe: Neon-lit pink Ganesha shrine that buzzes with worshippers and fortune stalls till late night
tip: Free. Best after 9pm, then walk to Huai Khwang Night Market. Bring a marigold garland and fruit

name: Wat Hua Lamphong (coffin donation temple)
vibe: Make merit by paying for a coffin for someone who can't afford a funeral. Weirdly uplifting
tip: Donation around ฿500. Ruamkatanyu Foundation desk is inside. MRT Sam Yan exit 1

name: Teochew Cemetery Park
vibe: A 1899 Chinese cemetery where locals jog, dance and do aerobics among 7,000 tombs
tip: Free. Go around 5-7pm to see the evening exercise crowd. BTS Surasak, Soi Charoen Rat 3

name: Wat Khanikaphon (the Madam's Temple)
vibe: Temple founded by a 19th century brothel owner, with a gold statue of the madam herself
tip: Free, quiet and almost tourist-free. Combine with Chinatown street food. MRT Wat Mangkon

name: Wat Intharawihan (32m Standing Buddha)
vibe: A 32m golden Buddha towering over backstreets north of Khao San that took 60 years to build
tip: Free. Morning light is best for photos. 20 min walk from Khao San Road

name: Loha Prasat (Wat Ratchanatdaram)
vibe: The world's last 'metal castle': 37 black spires and a maze of corridors you can climb up
tip: Free entry. Climb to the top for Golden Mount views. Go near closing for soft light

name: Ban Bat (Monk Bowl Village)
vibe: Last alley where families still hammer monks' alms bowls by hand, the clanging guides you in
tip: Free to watch. Bowls from about ฿800. Go weekday mornings when workshops are active

name: Kudeejeen (Kudi Chin) Portuguese Quarter
vibe: Tiny Thai-Portuguese enclave with Santa Cruz Church and 250-year-old recipe cupcakes
tip: Free to wander. Try kanom farang at Lan Mae Pao. Cross-river ferry from Pak Khlong Talat

name: Song Wat Road
vibe: Bangkok's oldest trading street, now spice shops, street art and hidden riverside cafes
tip: Go late afternoon, end with sunset beers at Samsara on the river deck

name: Nang Loeng Market
vibe: A 1900 wooden market hall full of old-school Thai desserts that most tourists never find
tip: Weekday lunchtime is best, many stalls close by 3pm and on Sundays. Cash only

name: Santichaiprakarn Park & Phra Sumen Fort
vibe: Riverside lawn by an 18th century fort, sunset over Rama VIII bridge with buskers and fire jugglers
tip: Free. Come at sunset, bring drinks from Phra Athit Road. Closed Sundays per Time Out

name: Public View Point (Wat Arun across the river)
vibe: Free riverside spot with a postcard view of Wat Arun lit up at dusk, no rooftop bar prices
tip: Free, no booking. 2 min walk from Tha Tien pier. Arrive 30 min before sunset

name: Royal Barges National Museum
vibe: Shed full of giant gilded dragon-headed royal barges, hidden down a Thonburi canal alley
tip: Around ฿100. Reach by longtail or walk from Bangkok Noi. Extra small fee for camera

name: Wat Mangkon Kamalawat (fortune sticks)
vibe: Smoky Chinatown temple where you shake numbered sticks for your fortune slip
tip: Free, donation for incense. Try kau cim early morning before crowds. MRT Wat Mangkon

name: Sri Maha Mariamman Temple (Wat Khaek)
vibe: Technicolor Hindu temple with a midday Friday oil-lamp ritual right off busy Silom Road
tip: Free. Fridays are the big day. Shoes off, no photos inside

name: Kathmandu Photo Gallery
vibe: Tiny restored shophouse with a photography gallery upstairs run by photographer Manit Sriwanichpoom
tip: Free. 87 Pan Road, near the Hindu temple. Check the site for current show

name: The Jam Factory
vibe: Old warehouses turned design store, bookshop, gallery and riverside lawn under a huge tree
tip: Free to wander. Weekend markets and gigs sometimes. Cross by ferry from Si Phraya pier

name: Doc Club & Pub
vibe: 50-seat indie cinema plus cafe-pub showing documentaries and art films you won't find in malls
tip: Check the schedule online, tickets around ฿150-200. 2F Woof Pack, Soi Sala Daeng 1

name: Chalermla Park (Graffiti Park)
vibe: Under-bridge skate and graffiti park where Bangkok's street artists paint over each other constantly
tip: Free. Go golden hour for photos. Short walk from BTS Ratchathewi

name: Captain Bush Lane & Charoen Krung 32 street art
vibe: Hidden riverside lane of huge murals by the old colonial-era docks, a strong Instagram backdrop
tip: Free. Combine with River City and Warehouse 30. Morning light is softer

name: Butterfly Garden & Insectarium (Wachirabenchathat Park)
vibe: Free walk-in dome with hundreds of butterflies, hidden inside a giant park next to Chatuchak
tip: Free. Go mornings when butterflies are active; closed Mondays. Rent a bike in the park

name: Ko Kret Pottery Island
vibe: Car-free Mon island in the Chao Phraya with pottery villages, fried flower snacks and bike loops
tip: Weekends are livelier. ฿2 ferry from Wat Sanam Nuea pier. Rent a bike around ฿40

name: Bang Pu Seagulls (Bang Pu Recreation Center)
vibe: Thousands of migrating seagulls swarm a seaside pier, feed them and get surrounded
tip: Season roughly Nov to Apr. Go late afternoon for sunset. Free entry, bird food a few baht

name: Khlong Lat Mayom Floating Market
vibe: Local weekend floating market in canal-side orchards, way less touristy than Damnoen Saduak
tip: Weekends only, 9am-4pm. Hop on a ฿100 longtail canal ride through the orchards

name: Talat Phlu
vibe: Old Thonburi railway-side food district that comes alive at night, beloved by Bangkok foodies
tip: Go after 6pm, try the satay, khao mok and Chinese desserts. BTS Talat Phlu

name: Socials Sukhumvit (bar + bathhouse)
vibe: Cocktail bar downstairs, sauna and ice bath upstairs. Sweat, plunge, then have a drink
tip: From ฿200 (฿240 weekends). Closed Mondays. Bar can run till 2am on weekends

name: Dip Garden Onsen & Ice Bath
vibe: Outdoor Japanese-style onsen garden in Ari with 5C cold pools, 42C hot pools and a sauna
tip: ฿500 weekdays, ฿750 weekends. Mixed-gender, swimwear required. Go at night when it's cooler

name: ARAH Ice Bath & Sauna
vibe: Resort-style contrast circuit: 2C ice bath, magnesium hot tub, sauna and pool, no timers
tip: ฿890 for 3 hours with a welcome drink. Book the 6-9pm sunset slot. Bring swimwear

name: The Ice Bath Club
vibe: Big social sauna with aufguss sessions, ice showers and hot magnesium pool, a new way to meet people
tip: Drop-in passes and walk-ins OK. Towels and swimwear provided. Ground floor JLK Tower

name: RECHILL Thonglor
vibe: Ice bath, sauna, steam and hot tub circuit plus a dome for breathwork and sound healing
tip: From ฿750 per 2 hours, book via the app. Packages cheaper. Also has an Asok branch

name: Fickle Lifestyle (splash painting)
vibe: Throw and splash paint at a giant canvas Jackson Pollock style, messy and fun with a date
tip: ฿1,500 incl 60x80cm canvas and paint, 90 minutes. Wear clothes you don't mind ruining

name: PCHA Fine Art Studio (pottery)
vibe: Private wheel and hand-building pottery classes in a calm Ekkamai studio
tip: ฿2,500-3,000 per person, about 4 hours, reservation only. Pieces fired and ready later

name: Tentacles Workshop (make your own perfume)
vibe: Design a personal scent from scratch with a perfumer and walk out with your own 30ml bottle
tip: ฿3,000 per person incl. bottle. Book in advance. Great gift or date idea

name: Karaoke Manekineko Silom Edge
vibe: Japanese private karaoke boxes open till 5am, cheap enough for a spontaneous late-night session
tip: Promos from ฿100 pp for 2 hours with free soft drinks. Book on weekends. 4F Silom Edge

name: Teeshot Bar (Marriott Marquis Queen's Park)
vibe: Sports simulator bar: golf swing analysis, virtual football, a karaoke room and cocktails
tip: Book a bay for groups. Direct access from BTS Phrom Phong. Food is burgers and pizza

name: Red Bull Skate Park, Benjakitti Sports Centre
vibe: Free 1,400 sqm covered street skate park with murals, skateable even in the midday heat
tip: Free. Bring your own board. Busiest after 5pm when the local scene shows up

name: Preduce Skatepark & Shop
vibe: HQ of Thailand's first skateboard brand, with a covered street section and half bowl
tip: Open daily till 10pm. Buy or rent gear at the shop, ask about beginner lessons

name: Yokkao Training Center
vibe: Muay Thai gym for all levels, with pad work and masterclasses by real-name fighters
tip: Drop-in classes about ฿500-700. Beginners welcome, hand wraps sold at the gym

name: The Movement Playground (parkour)
vibe: Learn parkour vaults, rolls and landings in an indoor playground, like being a kid again
tip: Book a beginner class online. Wear grippy shoes. Good stress-buster after work

name: Wat Pho Thai Massage Pavilions
vibe: Get a Thai massage at the temple where the art was codified, inside the Reclining Buddha complex
tip: Temple ticket ฿300. Massage about ฿480 per hour. Go late afternoon to avoid queues

name: Thai Film Archive (Film Museum, Salaya)
vibe: Free film museum with a replica old-time cinema street, vintage projectors and outdoor screenings
tip: Free. Check the schedule for free weekend screenings. Far west, combine with Salaya cafes

name: Bike Bangkok by Night (Co van Kessel)
vibe: Cycle through dark alleys, lit temples and a flower market at night with a local guide
tip: Book online, around ฿1,500-2,000 incl. bike and snacks. Starts near River City
